standard_prerequisites.name: Wedderburn's theorem
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of a finite simple algebra as a matrix algebra over a finite skew field extension of the ground field, which reduces everything to modules over a skew field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence of module categories for a matrix algebra
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the equivalence between modules over the matrix algebra and modules over the skew field, under which the statements about simple modules, direct sums and dimensions are transported.

core_obligations: The reduction (proof lines 517-524): by the cited structure theorem the algebra is a matrix algebra over a finite skew field and its module category is equivalent to that of the skew field, so the uniqueness of the simple module up to isomorphism, the fact that finite modules are direct sums of copies of it, and the characterization of isomorphisms by dimension all follow because every module over a skew field is free.

Parts (4) and (5) (proof lines 525-532): the equivalence carries the skew field to the module described in the statement, which gives the description of the simple module and of its endomorphism ring, hence the endomorphism skew field and the identification of the algebra with the endomorphisms over it, while the statement about the centers is read off from the named lemma on matrix algebras and the dimension formula is immediate from the explicit shape of the module.

Part (6) (proof lines 533-534): a finite module is a direct sum of copies of a simple module by the earlier part, and its endomorphism algebra is therefore a matrix algebra over the same skew field, with the double endomorphism statement following from the same description.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to modules over a skew field using the structure theorem and the equivalence of module categories.
Read the uniqueness, decomposition and dimension statements off freeness over a skew field.
Transport the explicit description of the simple module to get the endomorphism statements and the matrix-algebra description of part (6).
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects the structure of modules over a finite simple algebra: a unique simple module, finite modules as direct sums of copies of it, isomorphism detected by dimension, the explicit matrix description with its endomorphism skew field, the identification of the algebra with the endomorphisms of the simple module together with the dimension formula, and the matrix-algebra description of the endomorphism algebra of any finite module with its double commutant (statement lines 497-515). The proof is a complete argument: the structure theorem and the equivalence of module categories reduce everything to modules over a skew field, where freeness gives the first three statements (proof lines 517-524); the explicit description of the simple module is transported through the equivalence to obtain the endomorphism statements and the dimension formula (proof lines 525-532); and the last statement follows because a finite module is a direct sum of copies of a simple one (proof lines 533-534). The non-formal content is the transport of the module-theoretic statements through the equivalence. The claim is H2.
